questions.prompt: Explain how the lab's in-memory task store protects its data while still offering full Create/Read/Update/Delete.

keyPoints.text: The task array lives inside the createStore closure, so outside code cannot reach it directly.
add() refuses blank text before creating anything.
keyPoints.quote: if (!text?.trim()) throw new Error("Task text is required");

keyPoints.text: getAll hands back a copy, so callers cannot change the store's own array.
keyPoints.quote: return [...tasks];          // return a copy so callers can't mutate our state

keyPoints.text: The defensive habits are: validate input, return copies, and return null explicitly when nothing is found.
keyPoints.quote: validate input, return copies, return `null` explicitly for "not found."

keyPoints.text: update spreads the changes and then re-asserts protected fields so a client cannot overwrite ids or timestamps.
keyPoints.quote: re-assert protected fields — is how real APIs prevent clients from overwriting ids and timestamps.

keyPoints.text: remove returns false rather than throwing, leaving the error decision to the caller.
keyPoints.quote: false = nothing deleted; caller decides if that's an error

questions.prompt: Why does the lab insist on immutable updates, and which copying mistakes does it warn about?

keyPoints.text: Three update shapes cover lists: spread to add, filter to remove, map plus spread to update.
keyPoints.quote: Memorize these three shapes: **add = spread**, **remove = filter**, **update = map + spread**.

keyPoints.text: These are exactly the shapes React state updates use, which is why they should become automatic.
keyPoints.quote: React state updates use exactly these patterns, so make them automatic now.

keyPoints.text: After an immutable toggle, the original list still reports the old value.
sort changes the array it is called on, so copy before sorting state.
keyPoints.quote: `sort` mutates in place, so copy first with `[...arr]`

keyPoints.text: A spread copy is one level deep; nested objects remain shared between copy and original.
keyPoints.quote: Spread copies the top level only; nested objects are shared references.

keyPoints.text: Shared nested references are behind most bugs where editing one thing silently changes another.
keyPoints.quote: where "changing one thing changed another" trace back to this.

questions.prompt: Explain optimistic updates with rollback and the network-failure facts that make them necessary.

keyPoints.text: The UI changes locally first, persists in the background, and rolls back if the save fails.
keyPoints.quote: update locally first, persist in the background, roll back on failure.

keyPoints.text: Rollback is cheap because the pre-change array was never mutated and still exists.
keyPoints.quote: the old array still exists untouched because we never mutated it.

keyPoints.text: On a failed save the code re-renders the original list.
keyPoints.quote: render(original); // save failed -> restore the truth

keyPoints.text: fetch rejects only for network failures, so HTTP errors must be detected by checking res.ok.
keyPoints.quote: fetch only REJECTS on network failure.

keyPoints.text: Networks are unreliable, which is why retry loops with a delay are a standard resilience pattern.
When parallel requests are combined, a single rejection fails the whole Promise.all.
keyPoints.quote: If ANY promise rejects, Promise.all rejects immediately with that error.
